title: Astrid and the Playlist
premise: Ansel Eastwick, seventeen, holds his fractured family together on microwave dinners and denial while their mother works hospital night shifts. When the school's legendary ghost begins leaving notes addressed to him by name — written in ink that shouldn't exist — Ansel discovers the ghost is Astrid, a student who vanished decades ago and left behind a playlist that can replay the truth of what happened to her. To free her, Ansel must win two championships: the school's meaningless music competition where the playlist will be performed, and a far deadlier contest against the town's founding families who buried Astrid's story and are willing to bury anyone who digs it up. In the end, Ansel wins the stage but loses the cover-up war's final round — until he chooses truth over safety, exposing the founders at the cost of his own spotless record, and releases Astrid's spirit by playing her last unfinished song with his siblings beside him.
about_author: Silas Fairweather is the pen name of a former night-shift radio host who grew up in a mill town full of stories nobody would print. They write young adult novels about kids who fix what adults broke.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A chaotic morning: burnt toast, little sister Wren's lost permission slip, brother Theo's silence since Dad left, and Mom's exhausted dawn return. Ansel insists to everyone — including himself — that he has it handled. Emotional beat: loving exhaustion masked as competence.

chapters.title: The Note in Locker 114
chapters.summary: Ansel finds a note in his locker addressed 'Ansel' in shimmering ink that won't smudge or photograph. It says only: 'You hum when you think no one hears.' He assumes it's a prank by rival Marcus Hale. POV shifts briefly to Wren, who saw a girl in old-fashioned clothes near the music wing. Beat: unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: Astrid, Apparently
chapters.summary: Ansel researches the school ghost: Astrid Voss, a music prodigy who disappeared in 1974, scrubbed from yearbooks. The library copy of her competition program is razored out. His friend Priya, archivist-in-training, helps him find one surviving photo. Beat: first thrill of mystery overtaking fear.

chapters.title: Ink That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: The notes continue, appearing inside sealed textbooks and Theo's jacket pocket — always knowing things only family could know. Ansel tests the ink; it glows faintly under blacklight and smells like rain on old wood. Theo finally speaks: 'She knows about Dad.' Beat: the secret cracks open at home.

chapters.title: Side A
chapters.summary: Following the notes' clues, Ansel and Priya find a cassette labeled 'SIDE A' hidden in the auditorium organ bench. Playing it, they hear Astrid's voice layered over piano — and a second voice threatening her. The tape ends mid-sentence. Beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Principal Dray announces the annual Founders' Music Competition, which Ansel's class treats as a joke. But the notes insist: 'Win it. It opens the room.' Ansel, who quit choir after Dad left, must enter — meaning performing publicly for the first time in three years. Beat: terror of being seen.

chapters.title: Hale Family Values
chapters.summary: Marcus's grandfather Aldous Hale, head of the Founders' Trust, takes sudden interest in Ansel, offering scholarship money and warning him away from 'morbid local legends.' Ansel realizes the Hales know exactly who Astrid was. Beat: the enemy reveals its polish.

chapters.title: Wren Sees Her
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She meets Astrid in the empty band room — a girl made of static and song — and isn't afraid. Astrid can't leave the building and can't remember her own ending. Wren promises to help, then carries the secret home alone. Beat: innocence bearing adult weight.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for Ghosts
chapters.summary: Ansel assembles an unlikely band: Priya on cello, Theo grudgingly on drums, Wren on tambourine and morale. Their first rehearsal is disastrous until Ansel plays Astrid's melody from Side A and the room temperature drops — approval or warning? Beat: found family forming through failure.

chapters.title: What the Yearbook Didn't Say
chapters.summary: Priya uncovers microfilm: Astrid was set to expose that the Founders' Trust funded the school by laundering money through 'scholarships' that never existed. A week after her discovery, she vanished. Officially: ran away. Beat: justice outside the law becomes personal.

chapters.title: Mom Comes Home Early
chapters.summary: Mom catches Ansel sneaking back from the archives at 2 a.m. Instead of exploding, she breaks — confessing she took extra shifts to pay off debts Dad hid, and she can't lose another thing. Ansel almost tells her everything and doesn't. Beat: the cost of protecting people from the truth.

chapters.title: Side B
chapters.summary: Guided by a new note ('Ask the organ'), they find Side B: Astrid's recording of the Trust meeting, names and numbers clear — including a young Aldous Hale. The tape also contains her plan to hide it 'where only music finds it.' Beat: the weapon exists; now they must survive holding it.

chapters.title: The Second Championship
chapters.summary: Ansel understands the real contest: get Astrid's evidence heard before the Trust's centennial gala, when the founders will legally seal all records forever. The music competition is the only public event on that stage beforehand. Two clocks start ticking. Beat: stakes crystallize.

chapters.title: Marcus, Unplugged
chapters.summary: Marcus catches Ansel copying the tape and, instead of reporting him, admits his grandfather terrifies him too — and that Aldous keeps a locked room of 'school history.' Uneasy alliance forms over stolen practice hours. Beat: rivals becoming allies.

chapters.title: Static and Sabotage
chapters.summary: Someone steals Side B from Ansel's locker and slashes the band's equipment days before semifinals. Only the Hales knew where it was. Ansel spirals into blame; Theo walks out of rehearsal. Beat: lowest point — the team fractures.

chapters.title: The Room Where Music Finds It
chapters.summary: Astrid appears to Ansel directly at last, showing him a duplicate hidden inside the organ itself — she anticipated theft fifty years ago. She also shows him her final memory: not murder, but Aldous chasing her onto the roof in the storm. Beat: grief and fury fused.

chapters.title: Semifinals
chapters.summary: With borrowed instruments and Theo returning mid-song without apology (the Eastwick way), the band scrapes into finals. Aldous watches from the back, and afterward offers Ansel a deal: drop out, and the Trust pays for college — for all three kids. Beat: temptation priced in silence.

chapters.title: The Deal on the Table
chapters.summary: Ansel seriously considers it — college money means Mom sleeps, Wren eats, Theo breathes. Priya confronts him: 'You'd trade her twice.' Ansel visits Astrid, who tells him she doesn't need avenging, only hearing. Beat: choosing between survival and justice.

chapters.title: Finale, Part One: The Song
chapters.summary: Competition night. The band performs Astrid's unfinished composition, completed by Wren's ear and Theo's rhythm, while Ansel sings the confession lyrics Astrid dictated. Halfway through, every speaker in the building crackles with Astrid's recorded voice — the ghost is broadcasting. Beat: triumph with teeth.

chapters.title: Finale, Part Two: The Truth
chapters.summary: Mid-performance, Ansel abandons the setlist and plays Side B over the PA as the centennial gala guests arrive below. Aldous lunges for the soundboard; Marcus blocks his own grandfather. The founders' names ring through the school Astrid never got to leave. Beat: climax — exposure at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Loud and Quiet
chapters.summary: Consequences cascade: investigation reopened, Trust dissolved, Ansel suspended for the broadcast but celebrated everywhere else. Mom, furious and proud, finally hears the whole story. Astrid begins to fade as the town remembers her aloud. Beat: bittersweet victory.

chapters.title: The Last Track
chapters.summary: On graduation eve, the band returns to the auditorium to play Astrid's song one final time, finishing it together. As the last chord fades, the ink notes stop forever — and a single fresh page appears: 'Thank you, Ansel. Now go be fine for real.' Beat: release, grief transformed into inheritance.
